body: Makes sense – now we deffer calls to both in `gdextension.cpp`.

Or, actually, deferring removal may be problematic... If removal is deferred, then when we're unloading the extension (to reload it in a bit), the `memdelete()` on the editor plugin may happen _after_ the extension has already been unloaded, and so its destructor inside the GDExtension won't be called.

In your latest push, you switched to deferring the call to `EditorNode::add_extension_editor_plugin()` in its entirety (rather than doing the deferred call inside of that function), which I think is good. With that change, I think you can remove the bit that defers removal of the plugin, and it won't segfault anymore, because it won't pass the check to see if the plugin has already been added

Hopefully, there isn't anything else I'm not thinking of :-)

I actually tested it manually and EditorPlugin instance removed after hot-reload still had its lifecycle method called:

```bash

# First run
enter_tree called

# Hot reload 1
Initialize godot-rust (API v4.5.beta.custom_build, runtime v4.5.beta.custom_build)
exit_tree called
enter_tree called

# Hot reload 2
Initialize godot-rust (API v4.5.beta.custom_build, runtime v4.5.beta.custom_build)
exit_tree called
enter_tree called

# Remove EditorPlugin class – destructor is not being called, no error is being displayed as well.
Initialize godot-rust (API v4.5.beta.custom_build, runtime v4.5.beta.custom_build)

# Add EditorPlugin class.
Initialize godot-rust (API v4.5.beta.custom_build, runtime v4.5.beta.custom_build)
enter_tree called
```

In general it seems to cause a lot of jank while working with classes that has been removed during hot reload while [aforementioned check](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c81fd6c51233a727da528cf7f74137d56b5d6efe/editor/editor_node.cpp#L3968) should be enough. (I'm not sure if I really want to dig into it :sweat_smile:)
